missions.title: ENERGY SCAN
missions.objective: Distinguish potential energy from kinetic energy.
missions.briefing: Read each situation. Still and in position, or moving? Lock in one answer for your company.

questions.label: SITUATION 1 / 5
questions.context: A ball is held still on a high shelf.
questions.explanation: Still object → potential energy. The textbook rule (Task 3): “A still object has potential energy.”
questions.source_reference: Deck Game 1 · built on Textbook Task 3 (still = potential, moving = kinetic)

questions.label: SITUATION 2 / 5
questions.context: A car is driving along a highway.
questions.explanation: Moving object → kinetic energy. The textbook rule (Task 3): “A moving object has kinetic energy.”
questions.source_reference: Deck Game 1 · built on Textbook Task 3 (still = potential, moving = kinetic)

questions.label: SITUATION 3 / 5
questions.context: A football is flying across the pitch.
questions.explanation: Moving object → kinetic energy: kinetic energy is the energy of motion.
questions.source_reference: Deck Game 1 · built on Textbook Task 3 (still = potential, moving = kinetic)

questions.label: SITUATION 4 / 5
questions.context: A box is resting on top of a tall cabinet.
questions.explanation: Still, and high up → potential energy: stored energy linked to its position.
questions.source_reference: Deck Game 1 · built on Textbook Task 3 (still = potential, moving = kinetic)

questions.label: SITUATION 5 / 5
questions.context: A ball at the top of a ramp is released and rolls down.
questions.explanation: Still, then moving: potential energy becomes kinetic energy. Remember this change — it is exactly what the crash report describes.
questions.source_reference: Deck Game 1 · built on Textbook Task 3 (still = potential, moving = kinetic)

missions.title: VOCABULARY BATTLE
missions.objective: Use the ten Unit 5 engineering words accurately.
missions.briefing: Ten words from the textbook. Complete the sentences and match the definitions.

questions.label: WORD 1 / 8
questions.context: Drivers ______ when they press the brakes.
questions.explanation: Decelerate = to reduce speed (to slow down). Textbook example: “Drivers decelerate when they press the brakes.”
questions.source_reference: Textbook Task 3, item 1

questions.label: WORD 2 / 8
questions.context: The ______ of this car is dangerously long.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance = the distance a vehicle travels before it stops. Textbook example: “The stopping distance of this car is dangerously long.”
questions.source_reference: Textbook Task 3, item 1

questions.label: WORD 3 / 8
questions.context: A still object has ______. A moving object has ______.
questions.explanation: Textbook rule: “A still object has potential energy. A moving object has kinetic energy.”
questions.source_reference: Textbook Task 3, item 2

questions.label: WORD 4 / 8
questions.context: When you kick a ball, the ______ moves it forward.
questions.explanation: Force = a push or a pull that makes an object move. Textbook example: “When you kick a ball, the force moves it forward.”
questions.source_reference: Textbook Task 3, item 3

questions.label: WORD 5 / 8
questions.context: A machine does ______ when it moves another object.
questions.explanation: Work is what a force does when it moves an object. Textbook example: “A machine does work when it moves another object.” No movement → no work.
questions.source_reference: Textbook Task 3, item 3

questions.label: WORD 6 / 8 · MATCHING
questions.context: Task 4 — four words, four definitions.
questions.prompt: Match each word with its definition.
options: a summary of an article, document, or other text
to move from one object to another
the unit of force that equals the force of gravity
the idea that a moving object's energy equals the distance it moves
questions.explanation: abstract = a summary of an article, document, or other text · work-energy principle = the idea that a moving object's energy equals the distance it moves · G = the unit of force that equals the force of gravity · transfer = to move from one object to another. All four must be correct to score.
questions.clarification: Science note (supplementary): the textbook's definition of the work-energy principle is simplified. In standard physics, the work done by a force equals the change in an object's kinetic energy (work = force × distance). That is why spreading the same energy over a longer stopping distance means a smaller force.
questions.source_reference: Textbook Task 4 (words and definitions A–D verbatim)

questions.label: WORD 7 / 8
questions.context: “Tests show that stretching seatbelts reduce the force and ______ that passengers feel.”
questions.prompt: Complete the sentence from the abstract.
questions.explanation: G is the unit of force that equals the force of gravity. The Results section says stretching seatbelts reduce the force and Gs that passengers feel.
questions.source_reference: Textbook abstract — Results (gap added for the game)

questions.label: WORD 8 / 8
questions.context: “Instead, most of the passenger's kinetic energy ______ to the belt.”
questions.prompt: Complete the sentence from the abstract.
questions.explanation: Transfer = to move from one object to another. Here, energy moves from the passenger to the belt.
questions.source_reference: Textbook abstract — Conclusions (gap added for the game)

missions.title: CRASH DETECTIVE
missions.objective: Check your understanding of the Stretching Seatbelt Test abstract.
missions.briefing: Background · Results · Conclusions. Decide whether each statement about the test is true or false.

questions.label: STATEMENT 1 / 7 · TEXTBOOK
questions.context: “Kinetic energy becomes potential energy in a crash.”
questions.explanation: The abstract says the opposite: “In a crash, a car decelerates quickly. This causes the passengers' potential energy to become kinetic energy.”
questions.clarification: Science note (supplementary): this is the textbook's simplified wording. In standard physics, a passenger riding in a moving car already has kinetic energy; in a crash that kinetic energy has to be absorbed — and the stretching belt absorbs most of it. For this unit, answer with the textbook's wording.
questions.source_reference: Textbook Task 2, item 1 (reworded for True/False)

questions.label: STATEMENT 2 / 7 · TEXTBOOK
questions.context: “Shorter stopping distances exert less force on people.”
questions.explanation: A slightly GREATER stopping distance exerts LESS force. Shorter distance = more force. Abstract: “The work-energy principle shows that a slightly greater stopping distance exerts less force on passengers.”
questions.source_reference: Textbook Task 2, item 2 (reworded for True/False)

questions.label: STATEMENT 3 / 7 · TEXTBOOK
questions.context: “Stretching seatbelts cause less work to be done on people.”
questions.explanation: Conclusions: “The new seatbelts reduce injuries. This is because less work is done on passengers.”
questions.source_reference: Textbook Task 2, item 3

questions.label: STATEMENT 4 / 7 · REVISION
questions.context: “Stretching the seatbelt increases the stopping distance.”
questions.explanation: Background: “With non-stretching seatbelts, the passenger's stopping distance is short. Stretching seatbelts increase this distance.”
questions.source_reference: Revision statement built on the abstract (Background)

questions.label: STATEMENT 5 / 7 · REVISION
questions.context: “The tests showed an increase in Gs.”
questions.explanation: Results: “Tests show that stretching seatbelts reduce the force and Gs that passengers feel.”
questions.source_reference: Revision statement built on the abstract (Results)

questions.label: STATEMENT 6 / 7 · REVISION
questions.context: “With non-stretching seatbelts, the stopping distance is long.”
questions.explanation: Background: with non-stretching seatbelts the passenger's stopping distance is SHORT.
questions.source_reference: Revision statement built on the abstract (Background)

questions.label: STATEMENT 7 / 7 · REVISION
questions.context: “Most of the passenger's kinetic energy transfers to the belt.”
questions.explanation: Conclusions: “Instead, most of the passenger's kinetic energy transfers to the belt.”
questions.source_reference: Revision statement built on the abstract (Conclusions)

missions.title: ERROR 404: ENGINEER ENGLISH
missions.objective: Repair sentences using comparatives, can, be going to, present continuous and the passive.
missions.briefing: ENGINEER.EXE is speaking bad English. Find the correct repair for each broken sentence.

questions.label: BUG 1 / 5 · CAN
questions.context: ✗ We can to make it safer.
questions.explanation: CAN + BASE VERB (no ‘to’, no ‘-s’, no ‘-ing’). Seen in the textbook: “How can you do that?”
questions.source_reference: Deck Game 4, bug 1 · structure from Task 8 language box

questions.label: BUG 2 / 5 · COMPARATIVE
questions.context: ✗ The new seatbelt is more safer.
options: The new seatbelt is most safer.
The new seatbelt is more safely.
The new seatbelt is safer more.
questions.explanation: Short adjective → -ER (never ‘more’ + -er): safe → safer, long → longer, great → greater. Seen in the textbook: “safer than our current models”.
questions.source_reference: Deck Game 4, bug 2 · structure from Task 7/8

questions.label: BUG 3 / 5 · BE GOING TO
questions.context: ✗ We going to test it.
options: We are go to test it.
questions.explanation: BE + GOING TO + BASE VERB — don't forget ‘be’. It expresses a plan or intention. Seen in the textbook: “Are you going to make the seatbelts stretch more?”
questions.source_reference: Deck Game 4, bug 3 · structure from Task 8 language box

questions.label: BUG 4 / 5 · PRESENT CONTINUOUS
questions.context: ✗ We're test it next week.
questions.explanation: Present continuous for a fixed future arrangement = BE + VERB-ING (+ time expression). Seen in the textbook: “We're testing it next week.”
questions.source_reference: Deck Game 4, bug 4 · structure from Task 7

questions.label: BUG 5 / 5 · PASSIVE
questions.context: ✗ Energy will transferred to the belt.
options: Energy will be transferred to the belt.
Energy will be transfer to the belt.
Energy will transferring to the belt.
Energy will is transferred to the belt.
questions.answer_display: Energy will be transferred to the belt.
questions.explanation: Future passive = WILL + BE + PAST PARTICIPLE. The focus is on the energy, not on who acts. Seen in the textbook: “…will be transferred to the belt.”
questions.source_reference: Deck Game 4, bug 5 · structure from Task 7

missions.title: FINAL CRASH SIMULATION
missions.briefing: System requires correct sequence. Put the four events of the stretching-seatbelt crash in order. Worth 300 EP.

questions.label: FINAL BOSS · 300 EP
questions.context: SYSTEM REQUIRES CORRECT SEQUENCE.
questions.prompt: Put the four events in the correct order.
questions.answer_display: SEATBELT STRETCHES → STOPPING DISTANCE INCREASES → FORCE ON PASSENGER DECREASES → INJURIES DECREASE
questions.explanation: The whole discovery, in order. Abstract: “Stretching seatbelts increase this distance. … A slightly greater stopping distance exerts less force on passengers. … The new seatbelts reduce injuries.”
questions.source_reference: Deck Final Boss · sequence taken from the textbook abstract
